identity.title: The varying mass distribution of molecular clouds across M83
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: To explore this question, we utilize archival data from the Atacama Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA), which can provide exceptional imaging data of this nearby galaxy.

question.value: Does the molecular cloud mass distribution in M83 show a truncation mass that varies with galactocentric radius, like the young massive cluster population?

evidence.quote: Here, we present a cloud-based analysis of ALMA CO($1\to 0$) observations of M83 to search for such a truncation mass in the molecular cloud population.
This project uses observations made by ALMA under project 2012.1.00762.S as proposed by Hirota et al.
we use the high-quality $^{12}$CO($1\to0$) data set

method.value: Inject 350 Gaussian clouds at 51 masses (1e5-1e6 Msun), 10 random offsets; fit logistic recovery function

results_numeric.quantity: Max cluster mass / max cloud mass

evidence.quote: The maximum cluster mass is about 1-2% of the maximum cloud mass.

findings_qualitative.value: Clouds in M83 follow Milky Way-like scaling relations except enhanced surface density and turbulence in the centre

evidence.quote: there are systematic variations in cloud properties over the face of the galaxy.

findings_qualitative.value: Toomre and Jeans masses exceed maximum cloud mass; interferometer-only Toomre mass comparable to maximum cloud mass

evidence.quote: Both the Jeans mass and the Toomre mass are larger than the maximum cloud mass across the disk.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular cloud masses have a truncation that decreases with radius like the cluster masses
claims.experiment: cprops cloud catalogue, radial-bin mass function fits
claims.result: Truncated power law preferred in inner three bins; Mc and Mmax decrease with radius
claims.finding: Maximum cloud mass scale decreases with galactocentric radius

evidence.quote: there is good evidence for a maximum-mass scale and this mass gets smaller with galactocentric radius.

claims.hypothesis: Maximum cluster mass tracks maximum cloud mass
claims.experiment: Compare Mmax,cluster from Adamo et al. with Mmax,GMC per bin

evidence.quote: The maximum-mass cluster is $1-2\%$ of the mass of the maximum-mass molecular cloud

claims.hypothesis: Cloud internal conditions explain varying cluster formation efficiency
claims.experiment: Radial trends in pressure, density, free-fall time
claims.finding: Cluster formation efficiency set by large-scale ISM, not cloud internals

evidence.quote: the average internal pressures, densities, and free-fall times remaining constant for the cloud population over the galaxy

claims.hypothesis: The cloud mass distribution is a Schechter function like clusters
claims.experiment: Fit Schechter, power law, truncated power law
claims.result: Schechter excluded in inner bins; outer bins not distinguishable
claims.finding: No good evidence for Schechter form

evidence.quote: There is not good evidence for this being the best representation of the molecular cloud mass distribution.

why_this_data.value: High-quality archival CO(1-0) of nearby face-on galaxy to compare with HST cluster work

evidence.quote: M83 is an obvious target for exploring molecular cloud properties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extrapolation method for mass correction rejected because it biases masses low by 25%

evidence.quote: The extrapolation method discussed in (cite: Rosolowsky_2006) leads to mass values that are biased low by 25%.

limitations_admitted.value: No short-spacing data; diffuse emission filtered; negative sidelobes

evidence.quote: The data are also likely missing flux from large-scale, diffuse CO emission (cite: Pety_2013).

limitations_admitted.value: Cloud blending in central region makes nuclear mass distribution suspect

evidence.quote: We should therefore regard the clouds in the $R_g<0.45$ kpc bin as particularly suspect

referee_caveats_inferred: Single fixed alpha_CO across a galaxy with a nuclear environment
Few clouds in outer bins limit model discrimination
Toomre mass depends on interferometer-filtered surface densities
